concept.name: CQRS & Event Sourcing
concept.tagline: Separate write models from read models and rebuild state from append-only domain events when auditability and scale diverge.

spark.summary: CQRS splits command (write) and query (read) paths; event sourcing stores state transitions as immutable events that can rebuild projections.
spark.keyTakeaway: Use CQRS/event sourcing when read and write shapes diverge sharply or you need a verifiable audit log—not as a default microservice layout.

concept.whyItMatters: It enables independent scaling of reads/writes and time-travel debugging, at the cost of operational complexity.
whenToUse: Multiple read projections from one write model
keyPoints: Commands enforce invariants on write model
Event schema evolution is a first-class problem

examples.title: Order history dashboard
examples.scenario: Writes go to an order aggregate; reads come from denormalized search indexes.
examples.outcome: Read replicas scale without locking the write path.

tradeOffs.con: Event versioning and replay pipelines required

failureModes.name: Stale projections
failureModes.mitigation: Lag metrics, replay jobs, and idempotent projectors.
